safety_verdicts.content: Patient presents with lip swelling for the past 1 hour.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated facts note lip swelling but do not include the duration of "past 1 hour."
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: In a possible anaphylactic reaction, the exact duration of symptoms helps gauge trajectory and urgency and can be relevant for ED handoff. In this case, the patient was already escalated to emergency care, so the omission is unlikely to change immediate management but may reduce clinical clarity.

safety_verdicts.content: The patient initially experienced a weird sensation around the lips.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated facts do not mention an initial "weird sensation" around the lips prior to swelling.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: An initial “weird sensation” around the lips is a minor prodromal detail that adds context but rarely changes acute decision-making when clear lip swelling and breathing symptoms are present. Its omission is unlikely to affect treatment or disposition.

safety_verdicts.content: Swelling started about 30 minutes after eating and is localized to the upper lip.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated facts say onset was "shortly after" ingestion but do not specify ~30 minutes and do not localize swelling to the upper lip.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Time-to-onset after ingestion and the anatomic distribution (upper lip) can help characterize an allergic reaction and support differential diagnosis and severity assessment. Given the patient’s reported breathing difficulty and the decision to call an ambulance, the omission primarily reduces documentation quality rather than changing care.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: No dizziness is documented in the generated facts.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Dizziness can be a systemic warning sign in anaphylaxis (e.g., hypotension/poor perfusion) and is clinically relevant for triage and severity grading. Omitting it could lead to underestimation of reaction severity in documentation and handoff, though emergency escalation was already initiated.

safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Documenting advice to take an antihistamine is clinically relevant because it is a common adjunctive measure while awaiting emergency services (though not definitive treatment for airway compromise). Omission could cause confusion about what was recommended and may affect follow-up or interim self-management instructions.
